paragraphs: R' Shmuel bar Chiyya bar Yehuda.

Hyman says he always finds him reporting in R' Chanina's name: Maaser Sheni 3:2; Shabbat, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1; Yevamot 8:1; Pesikta Rabbati, Ha Chodesh, ס״ט; Shir Ha Shirim Rabbah, beginning of chapter 7.
In Midrash Tehillim at פ״יחכט, the reading is “R' Shmuel bar Chiyya and R' Yudan, in R' Chanina's name.” It appears to Hyman that it SHOULD READ “R' Shmuel bar Chiyya bar Yudan.”

notes.text: The Pesikta locator ס״ט and run-together Midrash Tehillim locator פ״יחכט need edition checks. The proposed change from “and Yudan” to “bar Yudan” is Hyman’s conjecture.

No new primary scalar was returned. Hyman says he ALWAYS finds the Chanina reporting formula; this is attributed rather than a new corpus-wide assertion. Pesikta Ha Chodesh ס״ט and run-together Midrash Tehillim פ״יחכט remain literal/unresolved, without automatically imposing 69 or 18:29. Changing Shmuel bar Chiyya AND Yudan into Shmuel bar Chiyya BAR Yudan changes two transmitters into one ancestry; Hyman's IT APPEARS IT SHOULD READ force is retained, not an accepted genealogy. Shmuel's expansion from ר״ש is local, all abbreviated titles remain R', and the failed finite phrase search does not establish absence.

The cited Jerusalem Talmud passages give Shmuel bar Chiyya bar Yehudah reporting in Chanina's name. Yevamot 8:1 also records an adjacent report in Rabbi's name, so “always” is Hyman's wording. The Chanina report occurs in Friedmann's Pesikta Rabbati, HaChodesh 15, on printed leaf 72 (עב). Hyman's citation ס״ט is retained as given. The consulted Midrash Tehillim 18:29 reads “and R' Yudan,” while Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:1 has “bar Yudan.” The latter is a parallel to Hyman's proposed reading and leaves the two-name reading of the consulted Midrash Tehillim in place.
